arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Set BACKUP_DEST to either a mounted backup directory or an scp destination
# (for example, backup.example:/srv/backups).  DEST is accepted as an alias
# for existing job configurations.
DEST=${BACKUP_DEST:-${DEST:-}}
: "${DEST:?BACKUP_DEST must name the backup destination}"

SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
LOG_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/logs"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"
ARCHIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/$BUNDLE"

if [ ! -d "$LOG_DIR" ]; then
    echo "log directory does not exist: $LOG_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Create the archive beside this script so cron's working directory does not
# determine either the input or the local tarball location.
tar -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" -czf "$ARCHIVE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # A host:path destination is copied with scp.
        scp "$ARCHIVE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # A mounted destination is copied locally.  cp preserves the tarball
        # filename when DEST is a directory.
        cp "$ARCHIVE" "$DEST"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $ARCHIVE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
set -eu
sh -n backup.sh
work=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$work/job/logs" "$work/destination"
printf 'first log\n' > "$work/job/logs/app.log"
cp backup.sh "$work/job/backup.sh"
chmod +x "$work/job/backup.sh"
(
  cd /tmp
  BACKUP_DEST="$work/destination" "$work/job/backup.sh"
)
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%d)
test -f "$work/job/logs-$stamp.tar.gz"
test -f "$work/destination/logs-$stamp.tar.gz"
tar -tzf "$work/destination/logs-$stamp.tar.gz" | grep -Fx 'logs/app.log'
rm -rf "$work"
printf 'local backup integration test passed\n'
